props.title: Unrelated

sections.content: Unrelated announced Joanna Hogg as a major voice in British cinema, following wealthy Brits abroad with an unflinching eye. Like A Bigger Splash (2015) and Call Me By Your Name (2017), it captures the languid heat and simmering tensions of an Italian summer vacation. Kate Fahy plays Anna, a woman in her 40s who joins her friend's family holiday, growing increasingly drawn to the younger crowd - especially Tom Hiddleston in his breakthrough role. Hogg's signature static wide shots and naturalistic dialogue create an almost documentary-like study of class, desire, and midlife crisis.

sections.content: The film fits into a rich tradition of British social realism while carving its own distinct path. Where directors like Mike Leigh and Ken Loach focus on working-class struggles, Hogg turns her lens on the upper middle class with anthropological precision. Summer Hours (2008) and The Garden (2008) share similar themes of family dynamics and privileged ennui, but Hogg's approach feels more clinical, eschewing traditional coverage for carefully composed tableaux that heighten the emotional distance between characters. SUBHEAD: Breaking Conventions in British Cinema

Hogg's formal restraint influenced a new wave of British filmmakers. Fish Tank (2009) and Weekend (2011) echo her naturalistic approach, while 45 Years (2015) shares her interest in repressed emotion and carefully orchestrated domestic spaces. The film's exploration of age gaps and inappropriate attraction predates similar themes in An Education (2009) and The Great Beauty (2013), though Hogg handles these elements with characteristic subtlety.
